curriculum.lesson_evidence: Balance is controlling the body's position over its base of support. A wide base (feet apart, more body parts touching the floor), a low centre of mass, tight tummy muscles and eyes fixed on a still spot all help balance. Weight transfer is moving body weight from one body part to another, such as from both feet to one foot. Use a mat or soft grass in a clear space, hold balances only as long as feels comfortable and stop if anything hurts.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point. Official wording for MA2-RN-01 is recorded in lesson-pipeline/sources/nesa-ma2-rn-01.json where applicable.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Tariq wobbles when he lifts one foot and looks at his feet. Write two cues to help him balance and say why they work.

FEEDBACK
Cues: 'eyes on a still spot' and 'tight tummy, arms out'. A still point helps the brain steady the body, and tight muscles and wide arms stop the body swaying.

WATCH FOR
Thinking balance is only about strong legs. Balance uses the eyes, the tummy muscles and a good base of support.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
On a mat or soft grass, practise four balances: two feet, one foot, a three-point balance (two feet and one hand) and a stork stand. Hold each for 5 seconds, record how long you held each and choose one cue to improve. Give an easier option for each, such as holding a wall.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

Use a mat or soft grass in a clear space, hold balances only as long as feels comfortable and stop if anything hurts. Now choose a different situation to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
